title: Czas przyszły · będę
note: Compound future: bedzie-helper + bare infinitive. Mirror image of a2_past_byc (that unit did the past of byc, this one does the future). TWO GIFTS made explicit in the intro: (1) the shape is already his -- a1_trunk_can taught modal + infinitive (Moge pracowac, Umiem plywac), so the only new thing is the helper, called out on slide 1 and again in a quiz explain; (2) the future has NO gender, so after a whole past block of bylem/bylam he types ONE form -- slide 2 is entirely this relief, with a bylem/bylam -> bede table, and quiz item 2 tests it directly. FENCED, must not appear anywhere: (a) the perfective future (napisze, zrobie, kupie) -- a completely different formation, B1; not mentioned, not hinted, and no item implies a second future exists; (b) the alternative past-participle future (bede pisal / bede pisala) -- one pattern only, and it would also hand back the gender the unit just took away. FORKS TAKEN: (i) the COPULAR future (bede w domu, bedzie dobrze) is NOT taught. 'bede byc' is not Polish, so the future of byc-as-copula has no place in a bede+infinitive unit; consequence, accepted: 'I will be at home' is not yet expressible, and no item implies it is. (ii) bedzie jechac appears exactly once (Uzycie 10). The idiomatic Polish future of jechac is the perfective pojade, which is fenced; the imperfective compound is correct and is what the course can currently express. (iii) GLOSS POLICY, extending the AGENTS past-gloss rule forward: dynamic-telic verbs (gotowac, czytac, kupowac, pic, robic) are glossed progressive -- 'will be cooking' -- because 'will cook' really maps to perfective ugotuje; atelic pracowac / mieszkac take plain 'will work / will live'. Slide 3 tells him outright that Polish has one form where English has two, so the progressive glosses do not read as a separate tense. Infinitives used are all in the taught pool; jechac comes from a2_jechac, which precedes this node.

intro.title: You already know this shape
intro.body:
Look at two sentences you can already build:

Mogę pracować. — I can work.
Umiem pływać. — I can swim.

A helper verb that carries the person, then a second verb left in its plain dictionary form. That is the whole shape, and you have had it since A1.

The future is that same shape with a new helper. Swap mogę for będę and you are talking about tomorrow:

Mogę pracować. — I can work.
Będę pracować. — I will work.

So there is only one new thing in this unit: six forms of the helper.
intro.body_pl: Jak mogę / umiem + bezokolicznik. Nowy jest tylko pomocnik: będę.

intro.title: The future has no gender — none at all
intro.body:
In the past you had to choose every time: byłem if a man is speaking, byłam if a woman is. Two forms for one English word.

The future does not do that. Będę is będę. A man says it, a woman says it, and it is spelled the same both times. There is no male form and no female form to pick between — for any of the six persons.

After a whole block of byłem / byłam / byłeś / byłaś, this is a real rest. Six forms, and that is the end of the list.
intro.body_pl: Czas przeszły: byłem / byłam. Czas przyszły: będę — jeden kształt dla wszystkich.

intro.title: The second verb never changes
intro.body:
Only the helper takes a person ending. The verb after it stays exactly as you find it in a dictionary — pracować, czytać, gotować, pić, kupować, mieszkać, robić.

Będę pracować. ✓
Będę pracuję. ✗ — two person endings, one too many. Same mistake as saying Mogę pracuję.

One more thing worth knowing: English splits this in two — I will work and I will be working. Polish does not. Będę pracować covers both, and you never have to choose.
intro.body_pl: Osobę niesie tylko pomocnik. Drugi czasownik = bezokolicznik, zawsze.

examples.en: We will live in the city.
The children will be drinking milk.

intro.title: Saying when
intro.body:
Two time words you already have put the sentence firmly in the future: jutro (tomorrow) and w weekend (at the weekend).

Put one at the front, exactly where you put wczoraj in the past, and the rest of the sentence is built the way you have just learned.
intro.body_pl: jutro · w weekend — na początku zdania, jak wczoraj.

examples.en: Tomorrow Mum will be cooking lunch.
At the weekend we will be reading a book.
What will you be doing tomorrow?

quiz.explain: jutro puts the sentence in the future, and the helper carries the person — ja takes będę.
There is no woman's form to look for. In the past you had to choose byłam over byłem; in the future będę is the only form there is.
mama is a she, so the helper is będzie — and tata would take będzie too. One form covers he, she and it.
rodzice is plural, so the subject is a they — będą.
Only the helper takes a person ending. The second verb stays in its dictionary form — exactly as it does after mogę.
The subject is ja, so the helper must be the ja-form. będziesz belongs to ty.

quiz.prompt: Wczoraj byłam w domu. Jutro ___ pracować.
quiz.explain: Same speaker, both sentences. The past made her write -am in byłam; the future asks for nothing of the kind — będę.

type_items.explain: One form only. A man and a woman both write będę — the future keeps no gender.
The past needed three here — był, była, było. The future needs one: będzie.
Helper first, dictionary form second — the same two-part build as mogę pracować.

use_items.prompt_en: Type: Tomorrow Mum will be cooking lunch.
Type: Dad will work in the office.
use_items.explain: będzie for Dad and będzie for Mum — the helper does not react to gender the way był / była did.

use_items.prompt_en: Type: At the weekend we will be reading a book.
Type: The children will be drinking milk.
Type: Tomorrow I will be buying bread.
Type: What will you be doing tomorrow?
use_items.explain: co takes the front, then the helper, then the dictionary form. The question word does not disturb the two-part build.

use_items.prompt_en: Type: My parents will live in the city.
accepts: Moi rodzice będą mieszkać w mieście.
Moi rodzice będą mieszkać w mieście

use_items.prompt_en: Type: Anna will be drinking coffee.
Type: Will you (plural) be cooking lunch at the weekend?

accepts: Czy w weekend będziecie gotować obiad?

use_items.prompt_en: Type: My brother will be going by bus.
use_items.explain: jechać goes in after the helper untouched, like every other verb — and autobusem still tells you the means of travel.
